summary_html: Agency chooses **Differential Response (DR)**/**Alternative Response**: engage **services without court petition** when safety permits. FFPSA and IV-B/IV-E prevention funding support voluntary, front-end help to avert removals.
authority_html:

- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — assesses safety/permanency outcomes in DR systems

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held the 'reasonable efforts' clause of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act does not unambiguously confer an enforceable federal right on the Act's beneficiaries and Congress created no private remedy, leaving enforcement to the Secretary's funding mechanisms and state judicial findings.
key_cases.relevance: Front-end prevention obligations under Title IV-E are enforceable administratively, not by individual families in federal court.
key_cases.quote: we think that Congress did not intend to create a private remedy for enforcement of the “reasonable efforts” clause

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the denial of qualified immunity to caseworkers who removed a chronically ill child from his home without a warrant or pre-deprivation hearing, holding their failure to offer reasonably available preventive services that would have eliminated the need for removal was objectively unreasonable.
key_cases.relevance: Directly supports an alternative-response duty: services capable of averting removal must be considered before the child is taken.
key_cases.quote: In light of these circumstances, Defendants' failure to provide the Roskas with preventive services to eliminate the need for removal was not reasonable

key_cases.case_name: RH v. State, Department of Family Services (In re DRS)
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed orders placing the children with their grandparents and their father rather than returning them to the mother, holding that whether the Department made reasonable efforts is determined case by case and that the record supplied sufficient evidence of efforts to prevent removal and of the children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion applies Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-3-429(a)(iv), which it notes requires clear and convincing evidence that reasonable efforts were made to prevent the initial removal, the front-end prevention duty at this node.
key_cases.quote: Reasonable efforts are determined on a case-by-case basis.

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us
